newsitem.title: USA: U.S. troops may go to Zaire next week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. troops may go to Zaire next week.

text.p: About 1,000 U.S. troops, including an Army airborne battalion based in Italy, could begin moving into Zaire next week in a humanitarian mission to aid refugees, a senior Pentagon official said on Wednesday.

"Troops could be flowing into place sometime next week," said the official, who added that senior White House and Defence Department officials would go to the United Nations on Thursday to discuss the aid mission.

The official, who asked not to be identified, told reporters that between 3,000 and 4,000 U.S. troops were likely to be involved in an international military force, but only about 1,000 would go to Zaire while others would go to nearby countries to help establish a humanitarian airlift into Zaire.

The 1,000 troops, including about 600 red-beret troops of the 1st Battalion of the 508th Airborne Infantry Regiment based at Vicenza, Italy, will go to Goma in eastern Zaire to secure the airport and set up a refugee corridor of about 2 miles (3 km) from Goma to the town of Gisenyi in neighbouring Rwanda.

He said White House National Security Adviser Anthony Lake, Defence Undersecretary Walter Slocombe and Air Force Lt. Gen. Peter Pace, who is director of operations for the Joint Chiefs of Staff, would go to the United Nations on Thursday to discuss the mission with Canadian and other officials.

"I think it is unlikely they (troops) could be going before next week sometime," the official told reporters, adding that British and French troops would also take part along with Canadian forces under the overall command of Canadian Army Lt. Gen. Maurice Baril.
